Introduction to Astha Jain UPSC AIR 9

Astha Jain achieved an All India Rank 9 in the UPSC Civil Services Examination 2025. This achievement highlights her exceptional dedication and strategic preparation. Her story serves as a significant motivation for civil services aspirants nationwide. Also, her disciplined approach led to her securing a top position in this competitive exam.
Astha Jain UPSC AIR 9 Biography

Astha Jain was born in Kandhla town, located in the Shamli district of Uttar Pradesh. Her childhood environment greatly valued education and intellectual growth. Her father, Ajay Jain, works in business, while her mother, Mamta Jain, manages family responsibilities.

Astha’s early life featured strong academic discipline. She actively participated in student leadership and social activities during her school years. These experiences helped develop her interest in governance and policy discussions. This early focus eventually guided her towards preparing for the Civil Services Examination.
Educational Background

Astha Jain consistently showed excellent academic performance throughout her education. She completed her Class 10 and Class 12 from Scottish International School. Her foundational education provided a strong base for future studies.

For her undergraduate studies, she joined Miranda House College at the University of Delhi. She pursued a Bachelor of Arts degree, majoring in Political Science and Economics, completing it in 2022. This strong academic background in relevant subjects proved beneficial for her UPSC preparation.
Preparation Strategy and Support

During her rigorous UPSC preparation journey, Astha Jain made strategic choices. She enrolled in the Interview Guidance Programme at Vajiram and Ravi. This programme was crucial for preparing her for the final stage of the Civil Services Examination.

The Interview Guidance Programme focused on several key areas. It included structured mock interviews to build confidence and refine communication skills. The programme also helped with personality development. Furthermore, it involved in-depth discussions on important national and international issues, which are highly relevant for civil services. This comprehensive support helped Astha excel.
